title: Make Pico recording start reliable
goal: Ensure left-stick record-start events captured while a reset finishes are preserved for the next ready environment step, while stale movement and terminal events remain discarded.
doneWhen: Pico reset synchronization clears stale events before reset begins rather than erasing a queued record-start after reset finishes.
A left-stick start pressed during reset completion is consumed after reset, while non-start events are discarded.
Focused no-hardware tests cover the event-retention contract.
decisions: The control queue is sampled at Pico packet rate; pickle files intentionally omit record_start because CollectEpisode clears and reseeds the buffer on that event.

The existing post-reset queue clear can erase a left-stick event pressed during the long synchronous reset. Move stale-event clearing to reset entry and retain only record_start events captured during reset.
Movement remains blocked by the synchronous robot reset; retaining record_start schedules recording only after reset returns.

verification.summary: Release commits 990b273 and 8441320 improve record-start handling, add event diagnostics, align X discard with reset, and exclude the initial environment reset from the gripper reset signal.
checks: Python compilation and Git diff whitespace checks passed
Focused first-reset, reset-signal, and Pico episode tests: 3 passed
limitations: The raw Pico stream must still publish left_axis_click; this code cannot recover an input event absent from XRoboToolkit messages.
